picks.title: Asobi Asobase
picks.case: You asked for short and funny, and at twelve episodes this is the closest thing in the pool to Nichijou's particular register of escalating nonsense. It has the same trick of playing an utterly trivial stake completely straight until the animation itself gives up. Given how much of Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai is people over-planning tiny social manoeuvres, the games club should land.

picks.title: Hinamatsuri
picks.case: This is the deadpan end of what you already watch, and it is twelve episodes. The comedy comes from a psychic child and a career criminal negotiating domestic life, which is Nichijou's absurd-premise-played-flat approach with an actual through line. It also has the sincerity that Dandadan sneaks in between fights, so it should not feel like a change of diet.

picks.title: Mob Psycho 100
picks.case: This is already on your plan-to-watch list and it is the obvious next thing while you are part way through Dandadan. Both are supernatural action comedies whose real subject is a teenager trying to be a decent person with powers he did not ask for, and Mob Psycho gets there in twelve episodes. Since you have not started it, this is mostly a nudge.
